children: The dollar recovers as Treasury yields rise and oil prices push higher on worries over supply disruptions due to the Middle East conflict. The dollar is also supported by safe-haven flows and a weaker euro amid ongoing concerns about French debt. On Tuesday, the dollar hit a near three-week low against a basket of currencies following weak U.S. housing data. The dollar's falls also reflected rumors of progress in U.S.-Iran talks, which briefly lowered energy prices, but the move faded overnight, Danske Bank's Jens Naervig Pedersen says in a note. The DXY dollar index rises 0.1% to 101.778 after falling as low as 101.506 Tuesday. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
